dedupe_keys.name: halem hydrodynamic route optimisation for vessels in dynamic currents

description: HALEM (Hydrodynamic Algorithm for Logistic Enhancement Module) is a Python package that optimises vessel routes through currents computed by a hydrodynamic model. It accounts for currents that vary in space and time, variable ship speed, minimum water depth and squat, and computes the shortest, fastest, cheapest or cleanest (lowest CO2) route; it does not model the inertia of the ship. It was developed by Pieter van Halem at TU Delft, and version 0.3.0 was deposited on Zenodo in August 2019. Coverage is generic: it works for any waterway or coastal area with a hydrodynamic model. The code is free under the MIT licence and available on GitHub and Zenodo, with documentation on Read the Docs. Caveats: results depend on the quality of the hydrodynamic model, and the package has seen few releases. It supports route planning for dredging and inland or coastal vessels under tides and river discharge, including low-water depth limits, and emissions trade-offs. It complements OpenTNSim for inland waterway transport simulation and is related to the EU inland fairway network graphs.
